status: Frozen before first execution; do not tune from observed scores
purpose: Test whether a curvature-bounded endpoint interpolation outer LP closes the inner-outer width gap at tractable cell counts
cell_boundary_rule: logarithmic endpoints, including both frozen support endpoints
method: One nonnegative mass at each rate-cell endpoint, retaining duplicate endpoint columns across adjacent cells; the equilibrium mass plus all endpoint masses equals the known G(0)=1. For each atom in a cell, barycentrically interpolate its two endpoint responses and bound its error by cell_width^2/8 times a uniform absolute second-rate-derivative bound, multiplied by cell mass. Apply the same construction to targets.
derivative_bound: For a piecewise-constant strain-rate segment (start,end,slope) and observation time t, upper-bound the absolute second rate derivative by abs(slope) times the integral of u^2 exp(-cell_left*u) from max(t-end,0) to max(t-start,0); sum over segments. For G20 use 20^2 exp(-20*cell_left).
valid_calibration_coverage_requirement: All 117 previously valid-calibration trials per truth/design must be feasible and include both true targets
rules: Use exactly the parent loading histories, calibration, observations, seeds, support, targets, and known initial modulus
Verify the interpolated true masses satisfy every noiseless observation and target envelope
Verify every feasible finite-grid inner interval lies within the new outer interval
Compare against the previous 96-cell outer bound and 192-rate inner diagnostic without changing either result
A gate pass demonstrates utility under frozen synthetic assumptions, not novelty or external validity
If the 96-cell method fails either coverage or both width limits, stop this endpoint-interpolation route for an independent P4 kernel-method paper
